unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision deletes the sentence in which Yankee self-esteem is flattered by the conviction that the Southerner is unfit for modern life. It also drops 'even in this respect.' The fear that two eighteenth-century types may be alike now has no premise to reverse.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'He was little more fit than the Virginians' still implies the Virginians' unfitness.

evidence.quote: No doubt the self-esteem of the Yankee, which tended naturally to self-distrust, was flattered by gaining the slow conviction that the Southerner
but Adams had begun to fear that even in this respect one eighteenth-century type might not differ deeply from another.
Adams had begun to fear that one eighteenth-century type might not differ deeply from another.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore a short version of the first draft's sentence: 'No doubt the self-esteem of the Yankee... was flattered by gaining the slow conviction that the Southerner... was as little fit to succeed in the struggle of modern life... but Adams had begun to fear that even in this respect...'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: 'He suspected two eighteenth-century types were equally unfit').
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Adams's self-irony disappears: he first condescends to Lee's unfitness, then recognizes it in himself. The comparison becomes a flat assertion rather than a self-incriminating discovery.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Yankee's flattered conviction cut, so 'had begun to fear' loses its turn

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'because, in days of violent political bitterness, it showed a certain amount of good temper.' The claim that Lee's request outranked any Northern compliment is left unexplained. Earlier, the revision also cut 'how thin an edge of friendship separated them in 1856 from mortal enmity.'
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'two young men so hostile' and 'No one was more obnoxious to them, by name and prejudice' still signal the enmity.

evidence.quote: which flattered Adams's vanity more than any Northern compliment could do, because, in days of violent political bitterness, it showed a certain amount of good temper.
He asked Adams to write his letter of acceptance, which flattered Adams's vanity more than any Northern compliment could do. The diplomat felt his profession.

unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required context for an essential beat; the first draft kept the clause.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The request's meaning, a Southerner trusting a hostile Yankee's pen amid sectional enmity, has to be inferred. This thins the point of 'The diplomat felt his profession.'
unresolved_should_improve.title: Reason the acceptance letter flattered Adams was removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft cut the sentence pairing Virginian and Bostonian in vice, which left 'neither' dangling. The revision places it right after a Southerner-only sentence. It also cuts 'while the Virginian became quarrelsome and dangerous,' the bridge to the knife-or-pistol image.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The next clause, 'the Bostonian suffered less than the Virginian,' soon resolves the pair.

evidence.quote: The Virginian was weak in vice itself, though the Bostonian was hardly a master of crime. The habits of neither were good
if one had only the social instinct. The habits of neither were good

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Insert 'The Virginian was weak in vice itself, though the Bostonian was hardly a master of crime.' before 'The habits of neither.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: residue of an authorized compression; an authorized cut does not excuse it.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The reader briefly stumbles over who 'neither' means. The escalation from drink to danger is compressed into a jump.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'The habits of neither' has no antecedent

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'The influence of Harvard College was beginning to have its effect.' His slipping from Mount Vernon Street, Quincy and the eighteenth century loses its stated cause.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Paragraph 13's 'Slowly it weakened the violent political bias of childhood' lets an attentive reader infer the link.

evidence.quote: The influence of Harvard College was beginning to have its effect. He was slipping away from fixed principles

unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: supports the essential beat 'He was slipping from fixed principles' and the plan's progression risk.

unresolved_should_improve.title: Concord drift no longer attributed to Harvard's influence

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision drops 'He found that he could not be this--or that--or the other' and 'Judges always ranked him beneath a rival... he believed the judges were right.' Both survived the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'to his own great astonishment' and the 'better orator' clause still frame the surprise.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'this--or that' sentence and the 'Judges always ranked him' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: writing met 'his own felt limits').
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Being elected over a rival loses its ironic reversal, and the closing 'array of judges' loses its earlier echo. The dash rhythm of the felt limits also goes.

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision drops the old man's debate whether education 'had not ruined him,' the qualifier 'disappointment apart,' and 'Possibly the fault was his.' 'Probably less hurtful' now stands as a bare institutional judgment.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'probably' survives, and V2 keeps the balanced tone.

evidence.quote: Sometimes in after life, Adams debated whether in fact it had not ruined him and most of his companions, but, disappointment apart, Harvard College was probably less hurtful
Possibly the fault was his, but one would like to know how many others shared it.
Harvard College was probably less hurtful than any other university then in existence.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Prefix 'disappointment apart,' or restore the 'Sometimes in after life' clause.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: supports the voice profile's recurring qualifiers.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: These qualifiers are the narrator's hedging self-implication. Without them the backhanded verdicts read as flatter and more certain.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Retrospective doubt stripped from the verdicts on Harvard and classmates

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'If Harvard College gave nothing else, it gave calm' preserves the core verdict.
